original.prompt: Consider the following statements about a proposal made by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2026:
items: It seeks to link BRICS members' central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to ease cross-border trade and tourism payments.
The RBI recommended that it be placed on the agenda of the 2026 BRICS Summit, which India will host.
The RBI favours private stablecoins over CBDCs because stablecoins strengthen capital controls.
original.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: The third statement is wrong. The RBI prefers CBDCs to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls. Digital rails are being pitched as a workaround after rupee trade settlement with Russia stalled.
original.source: The RBI prefers central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls.

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following statements about a proposal made by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2026:
items: It seeks to link BRICS members' central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to ease cross-border trade and tourism payments.
The RBI recommended that it be placed on the agenda of the 2026 BRICS Summit, which Brazil will host.
The RBI favours private stablecoins over CBDCs because stablecoins strengthen capital controls.
rewritten.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: India, not Brazil, will host the 2026 BRICS Summit, and the RBI prefers CBDCs to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls. The idea flows from the 2025 BRICS declaration in Rio de Janeiro, which called for greater interoperability between member countries' payment systems.
rewritten.source: It has recommended that the government place the proposal on the agenda for the 2026 BRICS Summit, which India will host later this year.
